meta.title: Earth2 graph v5.1
meta.what_it_is: A fixed reference world: big end events out to 2030 traced backwards through necessary conditions and likely precursors. Each day asks where the real world is tracking it. Neutral: no helped or hurt labels on companies.
meta.odds_unit: percent (0 to 100). odds_now is the chance the event happens by window_end.
meta.strength_rule: strength = (B - A) / (100 - source odds) when the board says the target goes from A to about B if the source fires; for trigger lifts, strength = lift points / (100 - trigger odds in the major's year). Capped at 1.

cascade_rule.move: target change = d x strength x sign
cascade_rule.fade_note: hop 1 full, each further hop multiplied by 0.5
cascade_rule.visit: each node at most once per run
cascade_rule.fired: pinned at 100 and never moved by a cascade
cascade_rule.window_check: an effect that would land after the target's window_end is dropped

meta.base_note: Odds are the read 2 board (Nov 22) plus the tree, driver model, 62 scorecard and majors page as sealed Nov 19 to 20. F2 is loaded at 39% so the sample run applies the Nov 22 update through the engine.
v5_1_changes: Fixed at the source: the board parser read 'by Nov 2027' as Nov 20, 2026, closing 21 rows; window_end, window_peak and odds_by are now right on every board row.
Fixed at the source: the horizon table was read two columns off, so odds_by on every board row was shifted; now read from the 2 mo to 3 yr columns.
Merged the rare-earth deep dive as merged on Nov 23 (31 nodes RD01 to RD35, 56 links, 21 new companies, 5 extended; RD27 runs from DA7).
Added P6, the shipping and canals end event.
Applied the Nov 23 read 3 board moves through the engine (second cascade_log entry).

nodes.label: Navier-Stokes: can a smooth 3D fluid flow blow up (develop an infinite spike) in finite time? Practical follow-on: AI fluid solvers that replace slow physics codes in design work.
nodes.odds_text: 85.0% by Dec 2030 (expected solve window 2026-09 to 2027-06, difficulty tier 5)
nodes.least_capability: A model that can search and formally check a long proof at scale (about 10,000 agents for days)

solve_status.detail: OpenAI internal model (about 10,000 agents, 88 hours) claims finite-time blowup for forced 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes, Clay statements C and D; 166-page proof plus Lean formalization that compiled. Mathematicians interviewed think it is correct but hard to read; whether a forced blowup meets the prize wording is unsettled; OpenAI will not claim the prize; Clay still lists the problem as active.

nodes.unlocks: Tells engineers that smooth flows with a smooth push can break down, so simulations can fail in specific regimes. The larger effect is on method: any precisely stated maths question is now open to machine attack for a few million dollars of compute. Direct gains in turbulence or aircraft modelling are expected only after human rewriting.
nodes.belief_line: If solved, people will believe machines can now settle the hardest open questions in maths on demand, and that research can be bought with compute.
nodes.window_basis: Proof exists; window is for expert acceptance. Practical fluid-solver gains are a separate 2 to 4 year lag.

arms_it_breaks.direction: raises the ceiling on what AI research agents are believed to do; pulls forward claims on other hard problems
supports the case for very large compute budgets; one result cost an estimated 6 to 10 million dollars
puts research mathematicians and quantitative analysts into the automation debate
feeds backlash from scientists: 25 Fields medalists signed a statement on misaligned goals (2026-09-11)
prompts re-checks of cryptographic hardness assumptions, since agent swarms can be pointed at them

unverified_items: Independent peer review of the 166-page proof

nodes.odds_text: 90.0% by Dec 2030 (expected solve window 2027-01 to 2027-06, difficulty tier 2)
nodes.least_capability: A regulator approving on standard trial evidence, whatever found the molecule

solve_status.detail: FDA accepted Takeda's zasocitinib (TYK2 inhibitor, psoriasis) under priority review with a target action date in Q1 2027; BioSpace describes it as an AI-designed molecule. No AI-discovered drug has been approved by a major regulator yet. Insilico's rentosertib (AI-found target and molecule) started Phase 3 on 2026-07-07 (320 patients, China).

nodes.unlocks: Shows AI-designed molecules clear the same safety and efficacy bar as any drug; moves AI drug discovery from promise to product revenue.
nodes.belief_line: If approved, people will believe AI can cut years off drug development and that AI-designed medicines are a normal product.
nodes.window_basis: Regulator date set; priority review approvals usually land on time.

arms_it_breaks.direction: speeds the drug pipeline; sets a regulatory precedent for AI-origin molecules
validates AI biotech valuations and pharma AI spending

unverified_items: Whether zasocitinib counts as AI-designed is disputed; it came from Nimbus Therapeutics, which is generally described as using physics-based computational design (not checked in this run). If it does not count, rentosertib's Phase 3 readout (likely 2028 or later) is the cleaner test.
Isomorphic Labs had not reported dosing a patient as of 2026-11-18.

nodes.label: Public factoring of a 1024-bit RSA number with the number field sieve on GPUs, using AI-written code.
nodes.odds_text: 75.0% by Dec 2030 (expected solve window 2026-12 to 2028-06, difficulty tier 2)
nodes.least_capability: AI-written GPU code for the number field sieve plus a large idle compute fleet

solve_status.detail: RSA-260 (862 bits) factored 2026-09-03 with a Devin-written GPU siever (about 13.5 GPU-years, about 400,000 dollars). RSA-896 factored 2026-09-19 with CADO-NFS ported to GPUs by Claude (up to 2,048 GPUs, about 10 days, about 30 GPU-years). RSA-1024 estimated at about 900 GPU-years, about 28 to 30 million dollars. No algorithm change; RSA-2048 unaffected.

nodes.label: ERCOT's audit of data-center grid requests (reports due about Dec 10, 2026) disqualifies, or sees withdrawn, 30% or more of the Batch Zero megawatts.
nodes.least_capability: Paperwork: developers who cannot show site control, equipment orders or a $50,000 per MW commitment drop out.
nodes.current_fact: ERCOT's large-load queue is about 474 GW, roughly 90% data centers; about 204 GW is eligible for Batch Zero; about 300 projects must prove site control and equipment orders and post $50,000 per MW. Reports targeted for about Dec 10. BNEF (Aug 5): up to 49.8 GW of data-center load could be delayed.

nodes.label: Rotating outages: a grid operator in a major US region (ERCOT, PJM, MISO, SPP or the Southeast) sheds firm customer load (EEA3) during winter 2026-27 or later.
nodes.least_capability: Weather: a 10-day wide-area cold event like January 2026 on a grid with thinner margins.
nodes.current_fact: Nov 18, 2026: NERC's 2026-27 Winter Reliability Assessment says all areas have enough supply for a normal peak, but wide-area extreme cold could cause shortfalls; winter peak forecasts rose in 21 of 23 areas, mainly from data centers; El Nino flagged as added uncertainty.
nodes.source: https://www.publicpower.org/node/31701

nodes.label: Interconnection waits stay long: the Berkeley Lab 'Queued Up' 2027 edition shows a median wait above 5 years from request to operation and more than 1,800 GW still queued.
nodes.least_capability: Status quo: studies and transmission upgrades move slower than requests arrive.
nodes.current_fact: Jul 1, 2026 (Queued Up 2026): 2,061 GW in queues at end of 2025, down 10%; gas 253 GW, up 86%; time to commercial operation exceeds 5 years where data exist; only 13% of 2000 to 2020 requests were built.
nodes.source: https://emp.lbl.gov/news/backlog-power-plants-seeking-transmission-grid-connection-eased-somewhat-2025-amidst

nodes.label: A top-5 data-center state (by planned capacity) or the federal government puts a binding limit on new large AI data centers in place: a statewide pause on approvals or grid connections, a hard cap, or a dedicated tax on large loads, enacted by statute or kept in force for 6 months or more.
nodes.least_capability: One governor's signature: Texas showed in August that a pause can run through the grid regulator and the permitting agency without a new law.
nodes.current_fact: Texas has paused data-center grid approvals and environmental permits since Aug 3, 2026, pending an audit (reports due about Dec 10). Nov 3, 2026: the Texas governor-elect, who takes office Jan 19, 2027, pledged a moratorium on all data-center approvals; governors-elect in Ohio, Georgia, Michigan and New Mexico also campaigned on a statewide stop or pause. About 40% of pending US data-center capacity sits in states whose new governors made that promise (Cleanview via Bloomberg, Nov 6).

nodes.label: The state clock: five or more states have a statewide data-center pause in force at the same time (now three).
nodes.least_capability: An executive letter to a state permitting agency, as New York, Texas and Oregon used.
nodes.current_fact: Three in force: New York (Executive Order 62, Jul 14, 2026, state permits for 50 MW and up held pending a statewide environmental review; GR1 FIRED verified), Texas (Aug 3, 2026, grid approvals and permits paused pending audit), Oregon (Oct 9, 2026, state air and water permits for new or expanding data centers paused until July 2027). Quorum (Oct 26) counts only New York as a formal moratorium; no state has one in statute. Five governors-elect pledged statewide pauses (Nov 2026).

nodes.label: Texas's new governor issues a statewide order pausing data-center approvals by Mar 31, 2027.
nodes.least_capability: A letter to the grid regulator and the environmental agency, as the outgoing governor did in August 2026.
nodes.current_fact: Nov 3, 2026: the governor-elect won 57% to 41% (unofficial). Oct 22 pledge: 'When I am governor I will issue a moratorium, a ban, on all data center approvals' until the legislature passes protections. Takes office Jan 19, 2027; the legislature meets in January. The outgoing governor's audit pause runs to about December.

nodes.label: The local clock: adopted local data-center moratoria in the US pass 500 (GatherGov count).
nodes.least_capability: A town council vote.
nodes.current_fact: Sep 16, 2026 (GatherGov): 632 jurisdictions took formal action since January 2026, 270 adopted, 25 extended, 9 rejected, 5 repealed; 1,030 discussed one. Nov 3, 2026: voters restricted data centers in all but one of 41 ballot measures (Redbud via Al Jazeera); Bloomberg counts 46 passed or on track, at least 17 of them outright bans.

nodes.label: A top-10 data-center state repeals or suspends its main sales-tax break for new data centers, or adds a dedicated tax or fee on large loads.
nodes.least_capability: A budget bill; tax breaks are easier to end than projects are to stop.
nodes.current_fact: Oct 26, 2026 (Quorum): Washington removed a replacement-equipment exemption, New Jersey cut about $250M of uncommitted AI and data-center credits, Maine excluded data centers from some incentives. Texas's outgoing and incoming governors both back ending data-center tax breaks in the 2027 session; incoming governors in Iowa and Nevada pledged the same (Nov 2026).

nodes.least_capability: A hearing and a whip count.
nodes.current_fact: Mar 2026: a Senate and House bill to halt data-center construction until Congress passes AI rules was introduced. Nov 17, 2026: House members renewed the call for a national construction pause; support in the next Congress is unclear. Cosponsor counts unverified.

nodes.least_capability: A press release naming the pause.
nodes.current_fact: Nov 6, 2026: Bloomberg Intelligence says as many as 10 GW of data-center capacity could fail to come online next year as planned. nodes.least_capability: An executive order and a lawsuit; durable preemption needs Congress.

nodes.label: AI is cited for 100,000 or more announced US job cuts in calendar 2027 (Challenger, Gray and Christmas).
nodes.least_capability: Cheap agent software good enough for entry-level office tasks, plus a slow economy that gives cover.

nodes.least_capability: Already in the ocean; only the index print is pending (early January).
nodes.current_fact: Nov 12, 2026 (CPC): El Nino Advisory; Nino-3.4 at +2.5C; strong to very strong El Nino likely through Jan to Mar 2027 (over 79%); about 60% chance the 3-month RONI tops +2.5C, a historic event, for Oct to Dec and Nov to Jan; expected to weaken in early 2027. Next update about Dec 10.

nodes.label: Palm oil squeeze: the Malaysian benchmark palm oil futures contract closes above RM5,000 per tonne.
nodes.least_capability: Yields falling 6 to 12 months after drought, as in past El Ninos.
nodes.current_fact: Nov 13, 2026: about RM4,462 per tonne, down from a RM5,018 peak in late August. Analysts see 2027 output falling 2.7 to 4.6 Mt as El Nino dryness hits from Q1 2027, mainly in Indonesia; Malaysian stocks hit a record in October.

nodes.least_capability: A one-line commerce ministry notice.
nodes.current_fact: Nov 6, 2026 (Platts): exporters brace for curbs on 100% broken rice; none announced; broken rice $336/t FOB, up 5% in a month. India's 2026-27 crop seen at 146 Mt, down 8 Mt, after a monsoon running about 15% short (Sep 18). State rice stocks hit a record 59.6 Mt on Sep 1.

nodes.least_capability: A hot, dry spring finish in eastern Australia.

nodes.least_capability: Forensics on drone wreckage.

discoveries_pace.method: 1) Rebuilt every problem's status at each of 1,699 commits of problems.yaml; counted the last move from an open-type status into proved, disproved or solved for problems still solved on 2026-11-22. 2) Parsed all 538 rows of the AI contributions wiki; 'new proof' = sections 1a to 1d with a full-solution (green) outcome, 'found existing literature' = section 2a with a full-solution outcome; counted unique problems by date of first such entry. 3) Joined the two to label status changes. 4) Rate = last full logged quarter; growth = half over half and latest quarter over quarter compounded. Scripts: /home/claude/e2v5/scripts/parse_wiki.py, transitions.py, trans_count2.py, pace_counts.py.
caveats: The wiki stopped on 2026-06-30, so AI attribution for 2026Q3 and 2026Q4 cannot be verified from the logged list.
On 2026-10-06 erdosproblems.com stopped showing statuses and solved counts; status updates now lag behind claims, so the 2026Q3 and 2026Q4 all-cause counts understate machine output.
The wiki says it is not a benchmark and has selection bias: easy or obscure problems fall first; absence of past progress can reflect obscurity rather than difficulty.
Status history contains same-day flip-flops (a status set then reverted); the count uses the last entry into a solved state, which removes those.
The April 2026 spike (30) reflects a batch of results from new OpenAI models, so quarterly numbers are lumpy.
Several big claims (OpenAI 100+ problems, Tier 4 97.6%) are company reports not independently checked.
discoveries_pace.pace_to_window_rule: Difficulty tiers: 1 = known method, weeks. 2 = known path, needs engineering, money or a regulator, 6 to 18 months. 3 = needs a new method plus validation, 1 to 3 years. 4 = needs new science plus scale-up or a large machine, 3 to 6 years. 5 = may be impossible or needs several unknown steps, 5 or more years with a wide window. For pure maths and algorithm targets, windows are cut by about half versus 2024 expert expectations, per the measured pace. For physical targets (drugs, magnets, batteries, fusion, superconductors), AI shortens only the search step; lab work, scale-up, trials and regulators set the window.
discoveries_pace.ladder_notes: Excluded as trophy problems with no near practical use: Riemann hypothesis (a proof would not break RSA or elliptic curve keys), prime gap conjectures, Hodge and Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer (rumoured AI work in 2026, unconfirmed). Navier-Stokes kept because the user listed it and because its follow-on is AI fluid solvers.
